content:
alex_j: Hey team, support ticket from AcmeCorp. They say streaming responses over SSE are getting cut off — last chunk missing and client ends up with invalid JSON. Full error: "Unexpected end of input" when parsing the streamed event.

sara_support: Customer reports it happens ~10% of requests, mostly long generations (>800 tokens). Happens across regions. They pasted a sample from their frontend: `EventSource` code and the parsed chunks.

alex_j: Pasting the minimal repro they sent (private):
```js
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-large', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ...' } });
es.onmessage = (e) => { try { const payload = JSON.parse(e.data); // sometimes throws
  console.log('chunk', payload); } catch (err) { console.error('parse error', err, e.data.slice(0, 200)); } }
```

sara_support: They see messages where the last event payload is missing closing bracket or `finish_reason`. Example of a truncated chunk they logged: `{"id":"req_xxx","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...and the final sentence end"},"finish_reason":`

emma_engineer: Thanks — I'm looking. Do we have server logs correlating to their request id? ticket includes request_id header `rwd-req-20240304-9b2`.

devon_oncall: Pulling logs now. @ingram_prod_sre do we have any recent runtime patches touching SSE flushing or keepalive? I remember a kernel change last week around chunked transfer flush frequency.

ingram_prod_sre: We rolled a tweak to the batching/kv cache flush pacing two days ago (deploy 2026-03-12). It reduced small-token stalls but might affect final chunk flush timing if the connection closes quickly. No explicit SSE changes though.

devon_oncall: Log snippet for rwd-req-20240304-9b2 (redacted):
```
[2026-03-12T18:22:03Z] upstream send chunk 1 size=2048
[2026-03-12T18:22:04Z] upstream send chunk 2 size=4096
[2026-03-12T18:22:07Z] client disconnected, connection_close_reason=RST_STREAM
[2026-03-12T18:22:07Z] finalizer canceled before flush, job_id=req-xyz
```

devon_oncall: Client disconnected with RST_STREAM before server confirmed final chunk. That would produce truncated output. Need to know why client closed. Could be client-side timeout or proxy (ELB/edge) idle timeouts.

alex_j: Customer says their frontend didn't call close(); their network trace shows the websocket/EventSource closed by browser with net::ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING. They use Cloudflare in front of their app (not ours) — could be intermediate.

sara_support: Customer tried direct to api.redwood.ai (bypassing their CF) and still saw the same behavior but at lower frequency. So maybe multiple factors.

emma_engineer: Two angles: we can (1) harden server to attempt an explicit last-chunk flush on connection close / signals, and (2) give customers best-practice client-side buffering + reconnect logic that replays partial delta. For (1), adding a graceful wait on FIN/RST might be feasible. For (2), provide example that re-requests continuation using `start_token`/`resume` id if available.

ingram_prod_sre: We need to be careful: waiting too long to flush could increase p99 latency. But a short grace window (e.g., 200-500ms) on receiving RST_STREAM might allow the kernel to drain. We already have logic to call `response.end()` when job completes — the issue seems the HTTP/2 layer sends RST before final write completes.

devon_oncall: Repro steps I'm using locally to simulate: Netcat hack to kill connection mid-stream:
```
# start server stream request
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." "https://localhost:8443/v1/stream?model=redwood" > /tmp/stream.out &
# after a few chunks, kill the curl process to simulate abrupt close
kill -9 <pid>
```
This reproduces truncation reliably. We can add unit that tries to `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` less aggressive to allow flush.

alex_j: Customer also sees missing `finish_reason` in the final choice, which cause their JSON schema validation to fail. Could we include a robust sentinel event at start (e.g., stream_id) and a final delta-less event that marks terminal even if last text truncated? That would allow clients to detect incomplete final chunk.

emma_engineer: We can emit an end-of-stream heartbeat `event: rwd_eos` with an empty data `{}` once model signals done, and set an `eos_id` header per request. If the client doesn't receive eos within Xs after last content, they can assume truncation and call a `/v1/stream/resume` with last token. Implementation notes: we need to ensure this is part of SSE contract and backwards compatible.

ingram_prod_sre: Also check gateway/proxy keepalive. I see our gateway (nginx/edge) has `proxy_read_timeout` 60s and `send_timeout` 30s in one region — that might prematurely close long streams. We rolled different defaults for some regions for perf.

sara_support: Action items for support: ask customer for full curl/network trace, whether they use Cloudflare/NGINX in front. Provide workaround: 1) use fetch + ReadableStream with retry/resume, 2) set longer client-side timeouts, 3) ensure upstream proxies allow long-lived chunked responses.

devon_oncall: Action items for engineering:
- emma, prototype `eos` sentinel event and server-side 300-500ms graceful flush on connection close.
- ingram, audit gateway timeouts for affected regions and align to 120s for `send_timeout` on streaming endpoints.
- add server metrics for `connection_closed_before_eos` with request_id tag.

emma_engineer: I'll sketch the sentinel behavior:
```
// SSE event at stream end
event: rwd_eos
data: {"request_id":"rwd-req-20240304-9b2","finish_reason":"stop"}

// client can look for rwd_eos to verify completeness
```
I'll put draft in PR and mark feature-flagged.

alex_j: Noting this for customer update. Sara, can you send a short reply with recommended workarounds and say engineering is prototyping a sentinel event + gateway change? Also request full env/CF/nginx info.

sara_support: Yep. Drafting reply now.

support-bot: [auto] Ticket #4521 escalated to oncall and eng. Tagging devon_oncall and emma_engineer.

devon_oncall: One more observation: many clients parse each `e.data` immediately as JSON. If partial chunk arrives split across multiple SSE messages, parse error hits. Suggest recommend incremental JSON assembly: append raw `e.data` to buffer, attempt JSON.parse only when you detect a closing brace or the `rwd_eos` event. Add code example for resilience.

alex_j: Good point — include that snippet in reply.

sara_support: Sent reply to AcmeCorp asking for traces and providing mitigation steps + ETA for engineering work. I'll post updates here when they respond.

ingram_prod_sre: I'll schedule a quick config roll next week to harmonize send timeouts across regions, and put a guard in the deploy to prevent regressions.

emma_engineer: PR: draft feature flag + unit tests for eos event and a 300ms graceful flush on RST_STREAM. I'll link once ready.

alex_j: Thanks all. Leaving this thread open until we have customer confirmation. Quick note: flagging billing impact — if clients frequently reconnect and replay, token counts could spike. Ask billing to monitor abnormal token spikes for ticket.

sara_support: Noted, pinging billing team separately.

devon_oncall: Closing loop for now. If anyone sees new similar tickets, please tag `sse-truncation` label.

alex_j: Great. :thumbsup:"
